headline: Wayve launches $85M employee tender offer at $8.5B valuation for its self-driving tech
summary: The UK-based self-driving AI startup is allowing employees to sell vested equity, part of a growing trend to retain talent in high-growth companies.
details: Wayve, a UK-based self-driving tech startup, is allowing its employees to sell a portion of their vested equity. The $85 million tender offer is being led by existing and new investors at the company’s latest valuation of $8.5 billion.
This valuation was established in February during a $1.2 billion Series D funding round. Major investors included Eclipse, Balderton, SoftBank Vision Fund 2, Microsoft, NVIDIA, and Uber.
This marks Wayve’s second employee liquidity event, following a similar tender offer in May 2024. That previous offer coincided with its $1.05 billion Series C funding round.

Tender offers are becoming a key retention tool for AI startups, providing employees with liquidity without waiting for a full company exit. This strategy aims to keep talent from moving to competitors or starting new ventures once options vest.

Other startups like Decagon, ElevenLabs, Linear, and Clay have also recently completed employee tender offers. These companies span AI agents, voice generation, project management, and sales automation.

The ability to provide employee liquidity stems from investors' eagerness to acquire more equity in these high-growth companies. Investors are betting on even greater future valuations, even when buying at a premium.

Wayve's autonomous driving system uses a self-learning, end-to-end neural network, diverging from traditional high-definition map reliance. Its software learns purely from data, mimicking human driving experience to create a 'general-purpose' AI driver.

The company has expanded its headcount to 1,200 employees over the past year in pursuit of this goal. Wayve plans robotaxi pilot launches with Uber later this year and integration into Nissan's driver-assist systems by 2027.

headline: Samsung teases a wider, boxier foldable phone in new videos ahead of Unpacked
summary: Samsung's upcoming foldable phone is hinted to feature a new, wider aspect ratio. Official teasers suggest a shorter, stockier design when folded, aiming for a true widescreen experience when open.
details: Samsung has released new teaser videos hinting at a significantly different design for its next foldable phone. The clips suggest a shorter, stockier form factor when the device is closed. This new proportion aims to deliver a more immersive widescreen experience when unfolded.

These official teasers precede an upcoming Samsung Unpacked event where the device is expected to be unveiled. Rumors about Samsung experimenting with a wider foldable have circulated, and these videos all but confirm the design shift. It remains unclear if this new approach will be a permanent change or a limited-run product.
